facts.WAL-C-FRAMEWORK: Lifecycle is a passive extensible framework, not a coding agent. PDSA is a non-normative external-agent scenario; Plan/Act policy, automatic back-edges and task choice remain outside VibeVM. A reference agent is a future campaign.
facts.WAL-C-EVIDENCE: Verification evidence is valid only for the exact tree/artifact/run identity measured. R7.5 may expose optional read-only requirements facts keyed by full `spec://…#fact` addresses. Authoring status, consumer adoption, edge provenance/provider freshness, lifecycle status and typed gap/staleness observations stay distinct. An external long-running agent may use them to understand remaining requirements and choose its direction; VibeVM exposes facts, not that choice. Absence of that adapter changes no lifecycle.
facts.WAL-C-ALGORITHMIC: VibeVM remains fully useful without an LLM. Paid enhancement is explicit per feature (`off|assist|required`), binds a provider lazily and never replaces the algorithmic baseline.
facts.WAL-C-MECHANISMS: Scheduled extension contributions answer when; sibling qualified mechanisms answer how. Builtins are replaceable providers. R4.0 extracts one pure registry kernel reused by lifecycle, compiler, workspace and later R8 selection; a second collector is forbidden.
facts.WAL-C-DEPLOY: Install materialises the dependency world; package creates portable artifacts; deploy reconciles named destinations through plan/effect/intent/verify/receipt. Clean never silently undeploys. Static skills, Agent Plugins, Cargo applications, client projections, `~/.vibe/bin`, custom installers and future system resources share this plane.

facts.WAL-C-GATES: Development uses exact affected tests. A touched gated Rust crate also runs scoped conform; new or moved source spec edges run specmap in the same atom. Full panel runs only at coherent batch/final boundaries.
facts.WAL-C-WIRE: Every machine wire starts from JTD + registry + corpus + codegen. Never edit `formats/EPOCHS.toml` or generated Rust by hand.
facts.WAL-C-WORKERS: Claudez is the default delegable execution lane while healthy; Opus/max and external Sol supply judgment or failover. Native Sol Ultra subagents are not an acceptance lane because each pays the enormous boot prefix; root reviews in-context. Root owns architecture, review, commits and gates. Accepted worktrees are reclaimed immediately.
facts.WAL-C-PANEL-DENOMINATOR: Current self-check runtime prints `[54/47]` because `STEP_TOTAL` counts lexical call sites while seven calls execute dynamically. Do not use that total as coverage evidence; tooling follow-up is queued in PROP-055.

p.WAL-NEXT: R7.4 is complete and green. Execute R7.5 in four atoms: reconcile the evidence/optional-provider and lifecycle vocabulary laws; add JTD-first exact evidence identity and a metadata-only requirements query; build the optional read-only `vibe-specdoc` + `vibe-facts` projection; then expose strict CLI/MCP query/control surfaces and prove them with a fake external PDSA orchestrator. No lifecycle-embedded agent policy, task heuristic or automatic back-edge. Resume R4 registry/transforms after those neutral adapters, per the implementation ledger.
